name: Kitsa, Otterball Elite
oracle_text:
Vigilance
Prowess (Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, this creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.)
{T}: Draw a card, then discard a card.
{2}, {T}: Copy target instant or sorcery spell you control. You may choose new targets for the copy. Activate only if Kitsa's power is 3 or greater.
blocked_sentences: {2}, {T}: Copy target instant or sorcery spell you control. You may choose new targets for the copy. Activate only if Kitsa's power is 3 or greater.

needs.what: copy_spell must be able to name its victim by a declared target -- a `target` key holding a target id, read through `ctx.target_sids` the way `counter` and `return_spell_to_hand` already read theirs, so a card can declare `targets: [{"id": "t1", "kind": "spell", "selector": {"any_types": ["Instant", "Sorcery"], "controller": "you"}}]` and copy that spell
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `copy_spell` takes only `amount`, `controller`, `new_targets` and `sid`. `sid` is a value expression, and the value language has no leaf that yields a target's stack id -- `{"binding": "sid"}` reads the sid a *trigger event* carried, which is why every shipped user of the op (storm, replicate, casualty, gravestorm, Jin-Gitaxias-style cast triggers) is a triggered ability sourced to the spell it copies. With no `sid` in the spec the op falls back to `ctx.bindings.get("sid")`, which on an activated ability is empty, so a Fork-style line would load clean and silently copy nothing. `counter` solves the same problem with its own `target` key (`spec.get("target", "t1")` -> `ctx.target_sids`); `copy_spell` needs that key. `snapshot` is no substitute: its `target` goes through `target_oids`, which keeps only object refs and drops stack refs.

notes: The rest of the card is expressible and was checked: vigilance is a printed keyword; prowess is the shipped idiom (a `spell_cast` trigger with `filter: {"not_types": ["Creature"]}` and a self-only `pump`); "{T}: Draw a card, then discard a card." is a `tap` cost with `draw` then `discard`; and the activation restriction "only if Kitsa's power is 3 or greater" is an ability `condition` of `{"cmp": ">=", "left": {"power_of": {"self_only": true}}, "right": {"const": 3}}`. Only the copy target blocks the card. No answer file was written, per the partial-expressibility rule.
